comparison: Both support C3AR1/C3ar1 expression patterns in macrophages/Kupffer cells (C1-C5). OpenEval provides detailed analysis of scRNA-Seq data sources, while peer reviewers implicitly accepted these foundational expression data without challenge. Peer result also includes C115, C116, C128 which relate to expression patterns.

Strong agreement on human transcriptomic data showing C3/C3AR1 downregulation in MASLD/MASH (C6-C17). Both evaluations support these findings from Suppli et al. 2019 cohort. OpenEval notes lack of statistical testing for MASH vs MASLD comparison; peer reviewers accepted without critique.

Both support GAN diet model characterization (C18-C34). OpenEval provides comprehensive assessment of body weight, composition, histology, and gene expression. Peer reviewers accepted model establishment as 'solid evidence' without challenging the characterization data.

Both support establishment of macrophage-specific knockout model (C35-C37, C187). OpenEval emphasizes the ~88% reduction in hepatic C3ar1 as evidence of macrophages as predominant source. Peer reviewers explicitly noted this as a strength. Peer result also includes C52 (gene expression).

Both support lack of metabolic phenotype differences in C3aR1-MφKO mice (C38-C44, C83-C84, C100). OpenEval details comprehensive metabolic phenotyping; peer reviewers accepted these findings as strength showing 'comparable liver metabolic phenotypes.' Peer result extends to C45-C46 and C103, C118.

OpenEval supports lack of liver pathology differences (C45-C51, C85-C86) in macrophage knockout. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN despite accepting overall negative findings, citing critical weakness: 'Insufficient data showing effects on liver macrophage phenotypes.' Peer result covers broader claim set including gene expression (C53-C62, C78, C104-C106, C122-C124).

OpenEval supports lack of transcriptional changes in macrophage knockout (C52-C62). Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN with same critical weakness about insufficient macrophage phenotype characterization, despite accepting the negative gene expression findings shown.

Both support lack of metabolic phenotype differences in C3aR1-KpKO mice (C63-C67, C87-C88). OpenEval notes findings parallel macrophage knockout. Peer reviewers accepted as part of overall 'solid evidence' that C3aR does not contribute significantly to MASLD pathogenesis. Peer result includes C107, C119.

OpenEval supports lack of liver pathology differences in Kupffer cell knockout (C68-C70, C89-C90). Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, applying same critical weakness about insufficient macrophage phenotype data to Kupffer cell model. Peer result covers broader claims including gene expression (C71-C76, C81-C82, C108-C110, C125-C127).

OpenEval supports gene expression findings in Kupffer cell knockout (C71-C76), noting C3ar1 reduction and lack of downstream changes. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN with same mechanistic characterization concerns, though accepting the negative findings.

OpenEval supports summary statements of negative findings from both knockout models (C77-C82, C103-C127). Peer reviewers support overall conclusion (C77, C79-C80, C91, C95-C99, C101-C102), stating authors 'provide solid evidence' and work 'rule[s] out the role' of C3aR1 in MASLD pathogenesis.

Both support comparison with whole-body knockout literature (C91-C99, C101). OpenEval notes contrast between cell-type-specific and whole-body knockouts is well-documented; speculation about non-macrophage cell types is reasonable but requires future investigation. Peer reviewers accepted this framing. Peer result also includes C102.

OpenEval supports comparison with Mamane et al. 2009 findings (C91-C99, C101). Peer reviewers support cited literature context (C92-C94, C163-C170) without challenge, accepting these as important comparisons for interpreting current negative findings.

Both support C128 regarding Kupffer cells as predominant hepatic source of C3ar1. OpenEval cites ~73-90% reduction in knockout plus scRNA-Seq data. Peer reviewers accepted this claim as part of expression pattern validation.
OpenEval supports C102 (minimal C3ar1 expression in hepatocytes/stellate cells) based on scRNA-Seq data. Peer reviewers accepted this as part of overall conclusion about cell-type specificity.

Both support diet model context and relevance (C171-C173, C179, C186). OpenEval cites supporting literature and notes diet composition. Peer reviewers accepted these methodological and contextual claims without challenge as part of scientific transparency.

Both support mouse strain and experimental design descriptions (C182-C185). OpenEval notes appropriate use of littermate controls. Peer reviewers accepted methodological transparency without challenge.

Both support discussion of potential compensatory mechanisms (C176-C178) citing Kong et al. 2023. OpenEval notes this remains speculative for current models. Peer reviewers accepted as appropriate scientific context.

OpenEval supports C175 regarding lack of sex differences in hepatic macrophage C3aR1 regulation. Peer reviewers accepted this contextual claim without challenge as part of broader methodological and background information.

Both support C188 acknowledging modest fibrosis levels as study limitation. OpenEval notes this may affect interpretation of fibrosis-related findings. Peer reviewers accepted this limitation as appropriate scientific rigor.

OpenEval supports sex difference observations (C31-C34) noting nonsignificant trends limit conclusions. Peer reviewers accepted model characterization broadly (C18-C34) without specifically addressing sex differences, rating overall characterization as supported.

Peer reviewers supported extensive cited literature claims (C163-C170) from Han et al. 2019 and other sources not separately evaluated by OpenEval. These provide context for complement system biology and prior findings.

Peer reviewers supported extensive background and methodological claims (C111-C162, C180-C181, C189) that were not grouped as separate results by OpenEval. These include complement system biology, MASLD pathophysiology, and additional methodological details.
